One thing to note is that these new ssid and conn_ap_mac sensors will only work when using the V2 update method, so at the moment only with orbi routers.
On other routers these sensors will always be None (since they always use V1 update method because it is less load on the router).
Can we check model before we create the sensors so we don't create sensors that never will update?
We probably can, will try to work on that tommorow
We'll hold this until we've merged the fix PR.
@MartinHjelmare since the fix PR is now merged, can this also be merged?

Ready to be merged.

issue_context.title: Netgear integration doesn't report certain attributes despite being available
issue_context.body: ### The problem I'm using Netgear Orbi (RBR50). The integration doesn't report the following info despite being available in debug logs: - Connection type (wired/2.4GHz/5GHz) - Signal strength - Link rate - Allow or Block status - SSID its connected to - MAC address of the AP its connected to Link type, link rate and signal strength all show up as separate entities but are disabled: ### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2021.10.0 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant Container ### Integration causing the issue Netgear ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/netgear/ ### Example YAML snippet _No response_ ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? `2021-10-06 22:39:26 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.netgear.router] Netgear scan result: [Device(name='Mi Desk Lamp 1S', ip='10.0.0.109', mac='xxxxx', type='2.4GHz', signal=94, link_rate='72', allow_or_block='Allow', device_type=24, device_model='Xiaomi Desk Lamp 1S', ssid='Area 51', conn_ap_mac='xxxxx')]` ### Additional information _No response_
comments:
Hey there @hacf-fr, @quentame, @starkillerog, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`netgear`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L344) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

You can just enable the entities for Link type/connection type, link rate and signal strength. So they are present.

The Allow or Block status, SSID its connected to and MAC address of the AP its connected to could be added as sensors if you actually need them (although I don't think they were there in the previous version of the integration).
Do you actually need any of those three?
In this PR I added those features, you can test it if you want: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/57226

> You can just enable the entities for Link type/connection type, link rate and signal strength.

Ah yes I see that now. Although they have to be manually enabled for each device? Even for new ones that join the network??

I think it'd be better if these were available as entity attributes as well, since it's much easier to see?

> Do you actually need any of those three?

As entity attributes, sure.
`get_attached_devices_2` calls also increases load on the router. If these sensors are disabled by default, does it make sense to probe the router with this every 30s? Can this be made configurable?

No you can enable/disable devices in bulk (all at once) if you go to the entities tab (go to integrations --> click on entities in the Netgear tile --> on the top left you can select all --> top right you can enable/disable in bulk).

Due to HomeAssistant architecture rules these things are not allowed as attributes and schould be there own sensors as it is now.

You can disable polling in the system settings of the integration and then you can make your own automation to call the update function at each desirable intervall you want.
The PR exposes them as separate sensors?? I understand entities that can be graphed be discrete, but for something so simple, it should be absolutely be available as attributes.
No they schould be separate sensors as per the HomeAssistant standards and rules.
